current_episode.title: From Finance Expert to MSP Voice: Building a Business and a Brand | Pax8 - The Athena Rebels Podcast Episode 10

guest.bio_context: Heather McDonnell-Alford is the owner of Counting Creators, an MSP finance company covering outsourced finance functions from mailbox management to compliance work. She niched down into the MSP space within five months of starting her business, having originally planned to serve YouTubers. She has spoken at major industry events including the MSP Show 2025, Pax8 Amsterdam, and IT Nation London, and has built her professional profile and speaking opportunities primarily through LinkedIn.

pending_qa.q: What is Heather McDonnell-Alford's advice for MSPs or professionals who want to start building a presence on LinkedIn?
pending_qa.r: Heather advises that you should never outsource your personal LinkedIn content because your brand is fundamentally you, and generic or AI-looking posts will not generate engagement. Her core principle is relationship first every single time — finding out about people, making warm connections, and commenting or messaging with genuine intent rather than leading with a sales pitch.

pending_qa.q: What does Heather McDonnell-Alford mean by 'share the scar, not the wound' when posting personal content online?
pending_qa.r: Heather's principle is that you should only share personal or difficult experiences publicly once you have processed them fully and reached the other side — the scar stage — rather than sharing raw, unresolved pain. She gives her own divorce as an example: she only spoke about it publicly after significant therapy and having settled emotionally with the experience, ensuring the content serves and helps others rather than expressing unresolved trauma.

pending_qa.q: How does Heather McDonnell-Alford handle self-doubt and imposter syndrome as a business owner with ADHD?
pending_qa.r: Heather acknowledges that having ADHD comes with a very harsh inner voice and an extremely high level of self-expectation, which can lead to being very hard on herself when things do not go as planned. Her coping strategy is to step away from the situation and call trusted friends within the industry who will hold her to account and provide a reality check, sometimes bluntly telling her that her self-criticism is unreasonable.

pending_qa.q: What advice does Heather McDonnell-Alford give to women who want to put themselves out there professionally but are afraid of criticism?
pending_qa.r: Heather's advice is simply to do it, but to do it with the right people around you. She acknowledges that criticism will come, often from unexpected sources including other women, and explains this as a scarcity mindset where people fight for perceived limited opportunities. Her response is to actively create space for other women — for example, introducing a woman she admires to a speaking event organiser — because in her view there is enough room for everyone.

pending_qa.q: What is Heather McDonnell-Alford's philosophy on cash flow management for MSPs?
pending_qa.r: Heather is emphatic that cash flow is the most misunderstood financial concept among MSPs, who often believe they are financially healthy simply because there is money in the account at the end of the month without looking at the bottom of the P&L. She advocates for a strict pot system — maintaining separate savings pots for corporation tax, personal tax, cyber investment, salaries, and other liabilities — to ensure funds are always available for known obligations.
